_comment: Max first-load JavaScript per route, transferred kB (gzip over the wire), 375 px mobile viewport, cold cache, production build (npm run build && npx next start -p 3140; node scripts/measure-bundles.mjs). Next link PREFETCH traffic is aborted during measurement (scripts/perf-prefetch-filter.mjs) because it made the same build measure differently under different machine load; with it blocked the figures are identical run to run. Re-measured 2026-11-14 after the lucide-react 1.70.0 upgrade: routes over their previous ceilings use the measured figure plus 10%, while passing routes keep their tighter ratchet values. Lab bytes, not Core Web Vitals. Enforced by tests/site/perf-budget.test.ts against a live production server: by the `site` CI job on every pull request, and by hand with PERF_BASE_URL set. Lower a number when a route gets lighter; raise one only by a deliberate, reviewed edit. /workspace and /admin/reviews keep the ceilings they had before the quotation work (222.2 and 164.6): measured on a clean production build under Node 20 with NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL set, as CI builds it, they are 219.0 and 154.1 kB. Two changes keep them there: the project panel's quotation section and evidence-ladder card are on-demand chunks, and the quotation words live in lib/cost-evidence-labels.ts so the reviewer queue does not ship zod (that took /admin/reviews from 182.4 to 154.1 kB). /workspace still ships zod because the workspace itself validates AI tool output in the browser (lib/ai/schemas.ts, lib/ai/tools.ts). When measuring by hand, kill every `next-server` process first: `next start` re-execs under that name, so `pkill -f next start` leaves a stale server answering on the port and you measure the wrong build.
